issues.legal_issue: A substantial delay in filing first appeals against a land-acquisition compensation award may be condoned when the claimants are entitled to compensation at parity with similarly situated landowners.
material_facts: The claimants filed first appeals 22 years after the Reference Court determined compensation.
The land was acquired in the same year as land for which similarly situated landowners had received higher compensation.
The High Court enhanced the compensation to the rate determined for those other landowners.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in condoning the delay because the claimants were entitled to just compensation at parity with similarly situated landowners.
issues.legal_principle: Landowners whose land is acquired are entitled to reasonable and just compensation at par with similarly situated landowners. Applying that principle, the Court relied on Deo Karan, which determined compensation for land acquired in the same year. The Court referred to the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as the acquisition context.

predicates.first_appeal_challenges_land_acquisition: Landowners filed a first appeal challenging compensation determined for acquired land.
predicates.substantial_appeal_delay: The landowners filed the first appeal after a substantial delay.
predicates.similarly_situated_landowners_received_h: Other landowners whose land was similarly situated received higher compensation.

issues.definition: When landowners substantially delay a first appeal challenging compensation but similarly situated landowners received higher compensation, the delay may be condoned.

issues.legal_issue: Landowners who did not appeal the compensation award cannot obtain compensation above the amount awarded by the High Court in an appeal brought by the acquiring body.
material_facts: The acquiring body appealed against the High Court's enhancement of compensation to Rs.149 per square yard.
The landowners did not appeal the High Court judgment seeking compensation of Rs.297 per square yard.
The High Court's award of Rs.149 per square yard had attained finality as against the landowners.
The landowners did not establish that their case was comparable to the case in which Rs.297 per square yard had been awarded.
For land acquired in the same year, Deo Karan had determined compensation at Rs.149 per square yard.
issues.conclusion: The landowners could not seek compensation above Rs.149 per square yard in the acquiring body's appeals, and the award of Rs.149 per square yard stood.
issues.legal_principle: A party that did not appeal an award cannot use the opposing party's appeal to obtain an enhancement beyond the award that has become final against it. The Court also found no demonstrated comparability with Nanak, and relied on Deo Karan for the rate determined for land acquired in the same year.

predicates.acquiring_body_appeals_compensation_awar: The acquiring body brings an appeal challenging the compensation award.
predicates.landowners_did_not_appeal_award: The landowners do not appeal the award seeking a higher amount.
predicates.landowners_seek_more_than_final_award: The landowners seek compensation above the amount awarded to them in the judgment that became final as against them.

issues.definition: When the acquiring body appeals, the landowners did not appeal, and they seek more than the amount awarded to them, they cannot obtain that further enhancement in the acquiring body's appeal.

issues.legal_issue: When a delayed land-acquisition appeal is allowed and compensation is enhanced, statutory benefits and interest need not be awarded for the period of delay before the appeal was filed.
material_facts: The acquiring body was a public body and beneficiary of the acquisition.
The landowners filed their first appeals 22 years after the Reference Court's judgment and award.
The High Court condoned the delay and enhanced compensation.
The High Court also awarded statutory benefits and interest for the period between the Reference Court's award and the filing of the first appeals.
The Court considered that imposing those amounts on the public body would create a financial burden and could increase project costs.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's judgment was modified to deny statutory benefits, including interest, on the enhanced compensation for the period between the Reference Court's judgment and award and the filing of the first appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Although the claimants could receive enhanced compensation, the Court held that the acquiring body and beneficiary should not bear statutory benefits and interest attributable to the delayed period, given the substantial delay and the financial burden on a public body. The statutory benefits and interest in question were those available under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_land_acquisition_compensation and public_body_benefits_from_acquisition and substantial_appeal_delay and enhanced_compensation_is_allowed

predicates.appeal_challenges_land_acquisition_compe: Landowners bring an appeal challenging compensation determined for acquired land.
predicates.public_body_benefits_from_acquisition: A public body is the acquiring body and beneficiary of the acquisition.
predicates.substantial_appeal_delay: The landowners file their appeal after a substantial delay.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_is_allowed: The delayed appeal is entertained and the landowners receive enhanced compensation.

issues.definition: When a public body benefits from an acquisition and a substantially delayed compensation appeal is allowed with enhanced compensation, statutory benefits and interest are denied for the period before the appeal was filed.
